historical_references.reference: The Puranas mention the Esharvansh or Aswamegha Vansha, a dynasty of horse-sacrificers, who claimed descent from Indra through the horse Ashvamedha.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, around 2nd Millennium BCE to 1st Millennium CE
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a collection of ancient Indian texts that contain various mythological and historical stories, teachings, and philosophies. The Esharvansh or Aswamegha Vansha refers to a dynasty of horse-sacrificers who were believed to have descended from Indra, the god of rain and storms, through the horse Ashvamedha. Horse sacrifices were an important part of ancient Indian rituals, and the Esharvansh rulers were believed to have performed these sacrifices to maintain the divine favor and ensure good governance.

historical_references.reference: The epic Mahabharata mentions Eshwara, also known as Rudra, as the presiding deity of the Eshvansh or Ashtavakra clan.
historical_references.context: The Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. In the Mahabharata, the Eshvansh or Ashtavakra clan is mentioned as being under the protection of Lord Shiva, who is also known as Eshwara or Rudra. The Eshvansh rulers were believed to have been blessed by Lord Shiva and were considered to be his devotees. The name Eshurvansh may have originated from this connection to Lord Shiva, who is an important deity in Hinduism.
